items.followUp: What is the incubation period, and when does it end?

rubric.why: Identifies the interval and its starting point.
rubric.description: It is a time interval beginning when a pathogen enters the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a time interval beginning with the pathogen’s entry.

rubric.why: Identifies the event that ends the period.
rubric.description: The incubation period ends when disease symptoms appear.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the appearance of symptoms.

modelAnswer: The incubation period is the time between the entry of a pathogen into the body and the appearance of disease symptoms.

items.followUp: How does a scientific theory become a law? Give one example of a scientific law.

rubric.why: Explains that repeated testing and supporting evidence establish the statement.
rubric.description: A theory that is repeatedly tested and supported by evidence is stated as a scientific law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning repeated testing and support by evidence.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of a scientific law.
rubric.description: One example is Mendel’s law of segregation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Mendel’s law of segregation.

modelAnswer: In the textbook’s simplified account, a theory that is repeatedly tested and supported by evidence is stated as a scientific law.
An example is Mendel’s law of segregation.

items.followUp: What happens to food in a vacuole after a lysosome fuses with it?

rubric.why: States what the lysosome contributes to the vacuole.
rubric.description: The lysosome releases digestive enzymes into the vacuole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that digestive enzymes enter or are released into the vacuole.

rubric.why: States the result of the fusion.
rubric.description: The enzymes digest the vacuole’s contents, carrying out intracellular digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the vacuole’s contents are digested.

modelAnswer: The lysosome releases its digestive enzymes into the vacuole.
These enzymes digest the vacuole’s contents, resulting in intracellular digestion.
